section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces concerns about appearance among young women in Western industrialized nations and identifies media, parents, and peers as social influences on body image. The present study focuses specifically on the role of peers and body talk between friends to examine whether different types of body talk predict how women feel about their bodies and whether these relationships can be explained by the object–process dichotomy. No studies or experiments are labeled (e.g., 'Study 1' or 'Experiment 2') in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: Quoted sentences from the section: "Research suggests that young women in  Western industrialized nations are concerned  with their appearance, and some researchers  identify the media (e.g. Gonzalez et al., 2013;  Groesz et al., 2002; cf. Ferguson et al., 2011),  parents (e.g. Stice et al., 1999; Unikel et al.,  2013), and peers (e.g. Clark and Tiggemann,  2006) as three social influences that contribute  to the development of body image concerns (Thompson et al., 1999)." and "Consequently, in the present study,  we focus on the role of peers and specifically  target body talk to examine whether different  types of body talk between friends might differentially predict how women feel about their bodies, and whether the relationships could be  explained by the object–process dichotomy."
